blocks.text: A multi-arch tag points to an image index that maps each platform (linux/amd64, linux/arm64, …) to its own manifest; each engine pulls the entry matching its host.

items: Built on Apple Silicon → arm64 → on an amd64 server: `exec format error`.
amd64 image on arm64 runs under emulation: slow, and some JIT/SIMD-heavy ML code crashes.
Missing wheels for a platform → pip compiles from source (slow, needs compilers).

blocks.text:
$ docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 -t ghcr.io/acme/api:1.0.0 --push .
$ docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/acme/api:1.0.0
$ docker image inspect -f '{{.Os}}/{{.Architecture}}' ghcr.io/acme/api:1.0.0

rows: Great for Go/Rust; limited for Python wheels

blocks.text: The classic image store holds one platform per tag, so `--load` of a multi-platform build fails; push to a registry or use the containerd image store.

Q: "Your image works on your M-series Mac but fails with exec format error in production. Why and how do you fix it?" A: "It was built for linux/arm64 and the server is amd64. Build in CI with `--platform linux/amd64` or a multi-arch buildx build, and verify with image inspect."

items: One tag, many platforms via an image index.
Build for the target, not your laptop.
Prefer cross-compilation or native runners over emulation.
